about: Place-image style test (Josh, 2026-10-14): linocuts read as stereotyped or dated about half the time, and Josh's hypothesis is that a different art style per city makes exploring less samey and keeps people enjoying the art rather than critiquing a repeated style. Each city's places try that city's approved card style (docs/mexico-version.md), plus an abstract version, on two places, next to the current linocut. Run: COUNTRY=es-mx npm run style-test. Output: style-test/es-mx/index.html (not committed). Round 2 (Josh, 2026-10-14): city style wins, but CDMX, Guadalajara and San Miguel came out too similar (soft, flat, pastel). Each gets a distinct technique; Oaxaca and Puebla are settled and skipped. Oaxaca back in round 2 (Josh): folk art dialled up, defined by alebrije patterning, dotted outlines and the Zapotec greca border. Round 3 (Josh, 2026-10-14): wider experimentation for CDMX: six different directions on the same two places.
rules: Contemporary Mexico: today's clothes and objects, everyday life; no sombreros, cacti, skulls, rebozos or costumes. Lettering: only the place's own sign, word for word; no other words anywhere, no dates, no 'HOY', no neighbourhood or city names, no slogans, no brand names or logos. Keep the main scene in the centre; nothing important near the edges.

ciudad-de-mexico.style: Risograph print in two inks, hot pink and teal, with visible grain, slight misregistration between the two colours and flat overlapping shapes; contemporary and urban

styles.riso: Risograph print in two inks, hot pink and teal, visible grain, slight misregistration, flat overlapping shapes; contemporary and urban
styles.cut-paper: Cut-paper collage: layers of coloured paper with visible torn and cut edges and small soft shadows between layers, like a paper diorama photographed from above; bright, playful palette of jacaranda purple, coral, teal and sunflower yellow
styles.ligne-claire: Clean-line comic illustration (ligne claire): even black outlines, flat colour with no shading, crisp detail, contemporary graphic-novel look; palette of jacaranda purple, coral, mint and warm grey
styles.screenprint: Screenprint gig poster: three bold inks (magenta, cyan, black) with halftone dot shading, slight off-register, strong graphic composition, paper texture
styles.diorama: Miniature isometric diorama: the scene as a tiny handmade model seen from above at an angle, soft clay and painted-wood textures, warm afternoon light, shallow depth of field like a tilt-shift photo
styles.line-spot: Single continuous ink line drawing in the style of an architect's sketch on off-white paper, with one bright spot colour (hot pink) filling a few shapes; lots of white space
styles.kahlo: Painting in the style of Frida Kahlo
styles.rivera: Painting in the style of Diego Rivera
styles.day-of-the-dead: Illustration in Day of the Dead (Día de Muertos) style
styles.shadow-box: Mexican shadow-box diorama: the scene built inside a small open wooden box painted in bright colours, with tiny handmade clay and papier-mâché figures and objects, photographed straight on with soft light; playful and handmade
styles.textures: Mexico City, highly textured: palimpsestic and monolithic tezontle stone, saturated and geometric walls, fluid and sinuous steel, chiaroscuro and dappled light under emerald canopies, sizzling and aromatic amber glow, choral and kinetic street life. Palette: tezontle red-black, electric pink, cobalt blue, marigold, emerald, amber
styles.roma-condesa: Contemporary Roma Norte and Condesa, Mexico City: leafy and upscale, architecturally accurate — 1920s–30s Art Deco and streamline apartment buildings with rounded corner balconies, ironwork and pastel stucco, Porfirian mansions with carved stone details, tree-lined avenues with planted medians under dense ficus and jacaranda canopies; today's specialty cafés, natural-wine bars and design shops, people walking dogs, cyclists. Clean, light, contemporary illustration. Palette: leaf green, jacaranda purple, soft terracotta, cream stucco, sky blue
styles.diorama-photo: Photorealistic tilt-shift photograph taken from a high angle, so the real street corner looks like a miniature model: very shallow depth of field, crisp centre and softly blurred top and bottom, real materials and textures, natural afternoon light, saturated true-to-life colour, real people
styles.diorama-model: Hyper-realistic museum-quality scale model photographed with a macro lens: real miniature materials (weathered stucco, real tiny plants, ceramic tiles, worn paving), lifelike painted figures, warm natural light, shallow depth of field; looks like a photograph of a real place
styles.condesa-real: La Condesa, Mexico City: Art Deco and Streamline Moderne buildings with rounded corners, geometric facades, stylized ironwork and cream stucco, under a dense green tree canopy. Photorealistic city street photography: crisp detail, true-to-life saturated colour, strong late-morning sun with deep shadows and dappled light; no haze, no pastel wash. Palette: leaf green, cream, terracotta, jacaranda purple, sky blue

oaxaca.style: Naive folk painting with bright saturated colours, flat perspective and careful small details, inspired by Oaxacan folk art and alebrije patterns. Palette: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise
oaxaca.colours: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise

styles.folk-shadow-box: Mexican shadow-box diorama painted as naive folk art: the scene built inside a small open wooden box, with tiny handmade clay and papier-mâché figures and objects, every surface painted in bright saturated colours with careful small details and alebrije patterns, flat perspective, photographed straight on with soft light. Palette: cochineal red, marigold, indigo and turquoise

puebla.style: Illustration in the style of a hand-painted Talavera tile panel from Puebla: slightly glossy glaze, visible brush marks, a thin decorative tile border. Palette: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green
puebla.colours: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green

guadalajara.style: Linocut print with bold carved black lines and wood-grain texture, strong contrast, in bright colour
guadalajara.colours: terracotta, teal, mustard and sky blue

san-miguel-de-allende.style: Mexican mural painting style: flat fresco look, simplified forms, strong rhythmic composition, matte plaster texture. Palette: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green
san-miguel-de-allende.colours: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green

styles.shadow-box: Mexican shadow-box diorama: the scene built inside a small open wooden box painted in warm colours, with tiny handmade clay and papier-mâché figures and objects, photographed straight on with soft light; playful and handmade. Palette: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green

abstract: Abstract colour-block composition: large flat overlapping shapes and a few confident lines suggest the place and the people in it, without detail; bold and contemporary; use the city's colours

notes: Round 3 picks (Josh, 2026-10-14): CDMX diorama most interesting, but should be more photorealistic; ligne-claire second. Shadow box as an alternative for Oaxaca or San Miguel.
